messages:
sara: quick sync — we need a concrete plan for exposing SM occupancy, per-GPU memory, and queue depth for both Hosted + Dedicated pools. stakeholders: runtime, infra, console, and sales (dedicated customers).

matt: agreed. current telemetry only exposes aggregate GPU_util_percent and resident_memory_mb per node. not enough for per-pool headroom or per-tenant billing.

anika: for Dedicated customers we need tenant_id label on memory and queue metrics (or at least pool id). privacy concerns if we attach full tenant ids to metrics in hosted prometheus — maybe hashed tenant or siloed metrics.

luis: runtime can emit the following prototypes: 
```
redwood_runtime_sm_occupancy_percent{pool="hosted-us-east-1",gpu_id="gpu-42",model_family="redwood-4x"} 72.3
redwood_runtime_gpu_memory_bytes{pool="dedicated-nyc-1",gpu_id="gpu-7",tenant_hash="sha1:abc123"} 12582912000
redwood_runtime_queue_depth{pool="hosted-us-east-1",route="text-gen",priority="standard"} 8
redwood_runtime_enqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.01"} ...
```
these are counters/gauges from the serving process. sampling at 10s.

sara: +1 on names but we need to standardize labels: pool (hosted/dedicated region), pool_id, model, tier (free/paid/enterprise), and an opt-in tenant_hash for dedicated. Also a "slice" label for SM occupancy context (e.g., current_seq_len_bucket) — because occupancy varies a lot by seq_len.

matt: worried about cardinality explosion if we include model and seq_len buckets. propose: model_family + seq_len_bucket (0-32,33-128,129-512,512+). keep tenant_hash out of hosted metrics.

anika: console team needs per-pool aggregations (avg occupancy 1m/5m/1h), 95th percentile queue depth, and headroom estimate: headroom = (1 - occupancy_p95) * num_gpus. also want heatmap by instance_type.

luis: telemetry side note: SM occupancy is cheap to compute (kernel time / wall time) but it fluctuates per-kernel. we should sample a rolling avg in runtime and emit a gauge every 10s with fields: sm_occupancy_avg_10s, sm_occupancy_p95_1m. runtime can maintain sliding windows.

sara: about queue depth — do we emit per-worker queue_length_gauge or a push per-pool aggregated queue histogram? per-worker gives better debugging but adds series. Maybe per-worker + a pool_aggregated_metric that infra aggregates.

matt: infra prefers pushing per-worker to statsd and letting our aggregator pipeline roll up to pool+model. avoids double work and lets us compute different rollups. storage cost is main concern.

anika: dashboards: minimal MVP: 1) pool overview (avg occupancy, memory utilisation %, queue depth p95, running requests), 2) per-gpu detail page, 3) dedicated customer view (if tenant opt-in) showing their memory and queues. Also alerting suggestions: occupancy > 90% sustained 5m => scale or warn, queue_depth > 50 => investigate backlog.

luis: about retention and resolution: keep 10s raw for 7d, 1m aggregates for 30d, 1h for 90d. downstream cost estimate: ~20-30% storage bump if we emit per-gpu+per-worker every 10s.

sara: decision proposals:
- metric names and labels as luis suggested with seq_len_bucket and model_family (matt's bucket scheme)
- runtime emits per-worker raw gauges every 10s, infra aggregator stores and produces pool-level rollups
- tenant_hash only for Dedicated and stored in a separate metrics cluster (compliance)
- console shows pool overview + per-gpu pages; dedicated customer pages hidden by entitlement flag
- alerts: occupancy_p95_1m > 90% for 5m (pager to eng-sre), queue_depth_p95 > 30 for 10m (pager to eng-platform)

matt: ok. can infra/telemetry team confirm aggregator can handle per-worker labels? @luis?

luis: yes, we already have sharded aggregators. need to add pool_id and seq_len_bucket to grouping keys. i'll open a PR to the aggregator config.

anika: console UX: can we surface headroom estimate as a single number and a timeline sparkline for the past 6h? also need an affordance to toggle include_reserved_capacity vs only_running.

sara: good ask. design + console will mock this. @anika please add a small mock by EOD Tue.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: telemetry-config branch pushed to ci-results/telemetry-metrics-185.

matt: action items:
- luis: PR for metric names + aggregator keys (due Thu)
- anika: console mock and alert UI (due Tue)
- sara: write brief telemetry contract doc and label scheme (due Fri)
- matt: coordinate with sales about tenant_hash opt-in policy and legal (due next Wed)

sara: if no objections by EOD tomorrow we'll lock naming and start the runtime instrumentation sprint. please DM if you have privacy questions about tenant_hash.

matt: thanks all. short follow-ups in thread ok.
